page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a shared-CPU virtual server belonging to the High Performance family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from an AMD EPYC processor on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing 1 physical core with 2 threads. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1253.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2318.46, both falling into the average tier. Conversely, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2253.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 4565.57. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, measuring 25.27 GB/sec for large block reads and 21.3 GB/sec for large block writes.

Due to the shared CPU allocation and lower memory throughput, this instance is not designed for high-throughput database operations or intensive multi-threaded computations. It represents a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for low-resource applications. Appropriate workloads include lightweight utility services, basic software development environments, small-scale testing, and low-traffic web serving.
